source.title: Distilled Pretraining: A modern lens of Data, In-Context Learning and Test-Time Scaling
source.authors: Sachin Goyal; D. Lopez-Paz; Kartik Ahuja

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests induction-style copying and in-context performance using a trigger-copy task in a bigram sandbox and contextual QA benchmarks, rather than the original head-level analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper measures trigger-to-copy accuracy and in-context benchmark performance. Its figures also report standard language-modeling and test-time-scaling outcomes, but those do not measure the claim versions and are omitted. The authors cite prior work for some induction-head characterizations; cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: In a 2–4-layer transformer sandbox, the study changes the training objective (distillation versus cross-entropy) and reports how well models learn induction-style trigger→copy (Fig. 1c/5c). That is a result on V5's dependence on the training setup. The 1B ICL benchmarks (context QA, needle-in-haystack, counterfactual QA) measure context reliance, not induction heads or loss over token index.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that distilled pretraining improves generation diversity and test-time scaling (pass@k) but impairs in-context learning, which they attribute to weakened induction heads. Their explanation is that soft labels help high-entropy mappings but add noise to low-entropy copying mappings. Token routing is offered as a preliminary mitigation. The induction-head attribution for the 1B models is asserted from benchmark performance, not measured at head level.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies distillation during pretraining and evaluates trigger-copy accuracy and contextual-task performance. It does not reproduce the original induction-head identification, composition, or training-phase measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: In-context-learning performance changes with training-data scale and with token-routing proportion: the reported 15% routing improves two of three tasks, while 30% improves one task.

fits_no_version.finding: In 1B LLMs, distilled pretraining's advantage on context-reliance benchmarks (context QA, needle-in-haystack, counterfactual QA) shrinks with data scale. It turns into underperformance at 1T tokens in the IsoData setting on needle and counterfactual QA. Entropy-based token routing partly recovers this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Soft-label distillation during pretraining weakens context-copying/retrieval abilities relative to standard next-token training when teacher and student see the same data.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says the full codebase will be released for reproducibility but gives no URL.
record.problems: The induction-style evidence is a trigger-copy task in a bigram sandbox, not a head-level causal or compositional analysis. ICL benchmark values relevant to the reported comparisons are largely figure-only; the text gives qualitative trends but no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows left out. Standard language-modeling and pass@k results were omitted because they do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: No head identification, attention-pattern analysis or previous-token-head composition; only trigger→copy accuracy is measured.
No abrupt-formation window, no coincident ICL gain and no loss bump is examined.
No attribution of ICL in large models to induction heads; the 1B benchmarks are not head-level.

Head formation itself is not measured, only copy accuracy. The training-setup factor tested is limited to distillation with an imperfect teacher; data properties are not varied for the induction task.

record.verdict_notes: No numbers are given in the text for Fig. 1c/5c or Fig. 3/7/11; all results are read from figures. No uncertainty is reported. The sandbox varies trigger counts (5/10/20), but results are not reported separately by count.

versions.untested_parts: Tests trigger-to-copy accuracy in a small Transformer sandbox, but does not identify individual attention heads or test composition with a previous-token head.
Does not test abrupt formation in a narrow training window, coincidence with an in-context-learning gain, or a training-loss bump.
Does not estimate what fraction of in-context learning in large transformers is attributable to induction heads, or measure loss falling with token index.
Does not test induction-head prevalence across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.

Tests effects of distillation, training-data scale, and token-routing setup on induction-style accuracy and contextual-task performance. Does not establish a general account of how data properties determine induction-head formation or whether in-context learning persists across other setups.
Does not distinguish few-shot task learning from repeated-token copying or test whether other mechanisms carry most few-shot learning.
Does not resolve whether induction-head formation comprises separate or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: Distillation Pretraining (student, bigram sandbox)
rows.size_stated: Student has 64-dimensional embeddings; models have 2–4 layers.
rows.stage_stated: Trained with knowledge distillation; student uses half the teacher's data.
rows.operation_detail: Trained the student with soft logits from a teacher on a trigger-token task where the target following a trigger is copied within the sequence.
rows.measure: Induction head accuracy (trigger → copy) across training epochs.
rows.value: Figure only; authors state that distilled models show a consistent drop in induction-head task performance.
rows.note: The experiment measures induction-style copying accuracy, not the formation or composition of identifiable attention heads.
rows.check: V1 link is wrong: no heads are identified and no previous-token composition is tested. The row bears only on V5. The dependence on training setup is present (a 'consistent drop' under distillation), so the state is observed rather than partial. Values are figure-only; the text gives no numbers.

relationships.condition: Small (2–4 layer) transformers in the bigram trigger→copy sandbox; KD (T=2, α=0.5) versus CE students on 8k sequences
relationships.reason: Distillation from an imperfect teacher lowers induction-task accuracy across training versus standard training, so induction learning depends on the training objective. The evidence is figure-only with no numbers (R1).
relationships.display_finding: Distillation from an imperfect teacher lowered induction-task accuracy throughout training compared with standard cross-entropy training.

relation.reason: The study directly compares copying accuracy under CE and knowledge distillation, testing dependence on the training setup.

tranche.reason: The distillation training setting supplies a result on V5 through controlled comparisons of induction-style copying, without reproducing the original head-identification and composition experiments.

source_check.notes: The evidence measures trigger-copy behavior rather than identifying induction heads. Appendix A.3 specifies a fixed held-out evaluation set of 4k sequences; exact accuracy differences are not stated.

statements.correction: This study: 2–4-layer transformers; 64-token vocabulary; 8k student training sequences; 16k teacher training sequences; KD temperature 2.0 and mixing coefficient 0.5 versus CE; consistently lower trigger-copy accuracy under distillation; no numerical accuracy difference stated.
statements.problem: The general claim about training-objective dependence is supported, but the passage lists R1 as evidence without describing this study's distillation comparison. Its numerical examples explicitly concern other studies and are outside this check.
